nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an algorithm on inputs of a type $\gamma$ whose running time $T_A(x)$ on each input $x$ is a natural number, let $D$ be a probability mass function on $\gamma$, and let $c$ be a natural number. If $T_A(x) = c$ for every input $x$ in the support of $D$, then the expected running time of $A$ under $D$ equals $c$.
nodes.title: Constant running time on the support gives that expected time

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an algorithm on lists whose running time $T_A(y)$ on each list $y$ is a natural number, let $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ be a list of length $n$, and let $c$ be a natural number. If $T_A(x_{\sigma(0)}, \dots, x_{\sigma(n-1)}) = c$ for every permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, then the expected running time of $A$ when its input is $x$ rearranged by a uniformly random permutation equals $c$.
nodes.title: Constant running time on all rearrangements gives that expected time

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an algorithm on lists whose running time $T_A(y)$ on each list $y$ is a natural number, and let $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ be a list of length $n$. nodes.title: Average formula for the expected time over random orderings, in the reals

nodes.title: Average formula for the expected time over random orderings

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an algorithm on inputs of a type $\gamma$ whose running time $T_A(x)$ on each input $x$ is a natural number, and let $D$ be a probability mass function on $\gamma$. The expected running time of $A$ under $D$ is the extended nonnegative expectation $\sum_{x \in \gamma} D(x)\, T_A(x) \in [0, \infty]$ of the running time, the sum taken over all inputs.
nodes.title: Expected running time

nodes.summary: For a list $x$, every list in the support of the uniform permutation of $x$ has the same length as $x$.
nodes.title: Rearrangements preserve length

nodes.summary: For a list $x$, every list in the support of the uniform permutation of $x$ is a permutation of $x$, that is, it has the same entries with the same multiplicities.
nodes.title: Rearrangements are permutations

nodes.summary: For a list $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$, the uniform permutation of $x$ is the probability distribution on lists obtained by choosing a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ uniformly at random and outputting $(x_{\sigma(0)}, \dots, x_{\sigma(n-1)})$.
nodes.title: Uniformly random rearrangement of a list

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
